text:
Topological Board Game used generative AI tools during development to assist with programming, documentation, store-page text, localization drafts, and design iteration. All AI-assisted material is reviewed and edited by the developer before being included in the game or store page.
The game does not use generative AI to create live player-facing content during gameplay. It does not connect to external third-party AI services during normal gameplay. Local robot opponents, rule-based analysis, search, simulation, and self-play/research tools may be included, but these are gameplay/strategy systems rather than live generative AI content systems.

Suno AI - Used for Music that is played in game
Chat GPT - Used for the billboards shown in game

I used Grok CLI for coding and all sprite generation. I use AI to debug.
There are AI generated videos in the tutorial sections.
AI was used to implement sound and music as well as menu assets and backgrounds.
No AI LLM is in the game. There is no real time AI asset generation or LLM streaming.

Generative AI tools were used to assist with selected static visual assets, such as artwork, store/library assets, and some icon-style graphics. These assets were reviewed, edited, and manually integrated by the developer. No generative AI is used during gameplay, and no content is generated by AI while the game is running.
Some background images and logos made with generated content using ChatGPT 4o, and Midjourney. A couple of audio tracks made with Suno.ai.

Generative AI tools were used during development to create and refine some pre-generated content, including UI artwork and icons, selected 3D models and textures, music, character and dealer voice lines, and localized text. Tools used include OpenAI image generation and Codex, Meshy, Suno, and Alibaba Cloud Model Studio. All AI-assisted content was reviewed, curated, and edited before inclusion. The game does not generate AI content at runtime or connect to generative AI services during play.

Some visual assets (character sprites and facial feature illustrations)
and background music in this game were created with the assistance
of AI generation tools. All AI-generated content was reviewed,
selected, and edited by the developer before inclusion in the game.
No AI content is generated live during gameplay.

This product uses generative AI only for some visual content, including in-game sprite images and promotional/store artwork such as capsule images, key art, logos, and character/instrument illustrations. AI is not used to generate live gameplay content in real time.

AI models have been used to validate, optimize, rank and test the puzzles and the simulation engine. Soundtrack is procedurally generated music using the same engine that simulates the electronics, powered by the C~ language.

The visual assets in Grim Looters — character, monster, item and card artwork, plus the store and marketing images — were created with the assistance of generative AI image tools and then curated, edited, and assembled by the developer. Some background music was AI-assisted. All AI-generated content is reviewed by the developer to ensure it is appropriate and cleared for use. No AI content is generated live during gameplay.

During the production process of "Pixi Vibe", AI-driven software was utilized in multiple stages, including technology development, early creative ideation, visual effect experimentation, and the creation of some art assets. These tools were solely employed during the game development phase. All content accessible to players is pre-produced, and no content is generated or modified using AI during gameplay.
You used ChatGPT-generated images for the logo, menu backgrounds, hangar art and store capsules.

The game does not use generative AI to generate player-facing content. Backgrounds and other visual assets were created procedurally, hand-authored, or edited by the developer. AI tools may have been used during development for efficiency, but no AI-generated content is live-generated for players.

Generative AI tools were used during development to assist with selected visual and audio asset concepts and production support.
All final assets included in the game were reviewed, edited, and integrated by the developer to ensure they are appropriate for the game and do not knowingly include infringing content. No live AI-generated content is produced during gameplay.

This game uses generative artificial intelligence to assist with story planning, writing, and editing, as well as to create character artwork, backgrounds, event illustrations, music, and selected sound effects. All generated content was reviewed, selected, revised, and edited by the developer before being incorporated into the game.
All AI-generated content was created in advance during development. The game does not generate new content while you play, and no player input or personal information is sent to any generative AI service.

Generative AI was used during development to create selected pre-generated audio assets used in the game, including background music and sound effects. Generative AI was also used to create selected studio logos and promotional artwork used on the Steam store page and in marketing materials.
No content is generated by AI during gameplay, and the game does not connect to any external AI services.

Some visual assets used in DRIDENT were created or assisted with generative AI tools and later edited, integrated, and adjusted by the developer to fit the game’s horror atmosphere, visual style, and gameplay needs.
Generative AI was used only as part of the asset creation and visual production workflow. The game does not use live generative AI during gameplay.

Portions of the game’s visual assets and text content were created with the assistance of generative AI tools during development. All AI-generated content was reviewed, edited, and integrated by the developer to ensure quality and consistency. The game does not use generative AI at runtime.

Some visual assets and parts of the code for this game were created with the help of AI tools during development. No generative AI is used during gameplay, and players do not interact with AI systems directly.
In-game textures were generated and enhanced via the use of generative AI. Large Language Models were used to generate and assist with the Code.

Some store and library capsule art was produced with image-generation tools
(SDXL and a chat assistant) using our own in-game screenshots as the input
image. The underlying game content -- models, textures, code, text -- is
authored by us without generative AI. All generated art was reviewed by us
before publication.

Some visual assets, concept art, promotional materials, sound effects, text drafts, and development support for Duskvein Survivors – Bloodline were created or assisted using generative AI tools during development.
All AI-assisted content is reviewed, edited, curated, and integrated by the developer before being included in the game or marketing materials. The game does not generate AI content during gameplay and does not connect to any external AI services while being played.

AI-assisted tools were used during development to help create certain store assets and to assist with portions of the program’s source code.
The shipped game does not generate AI content during gameplay and does not connect to external AI services.
Visual effects and imagery in the game are generated deterministically by the program’s code using mathematical and procedural rendering techniques (ASCII graphics and SDL-based visual effects). These systems do not use generative AI.

For this game, generative AI is used as an auxiliary tool in some parts of development and production.
It is used to create rough drafts of some of the images, text, and localization ideas used on the store page and in-game.
Final acceptance, editing, and quality checks are handled by the developers, and the content is released only after being confirmed for accuracy and appropriateness.
Please note that no content is generated in real time in response to player input within the game.

Generative AI tools were used during the development of Clean Your Garden
for part of the 2D art (bug illustrations, backgrounds, weapon and
achievement icons, and store art), to assist with writing code, and to
assist with translating the game's text into English. All of it was
reviewed, edited and integrated by hand.
The game does not generate any content with AI while you play: no model
runs at runtime.
---
Durante el desarrollo de Clean Your Garden se han usado herramientas de IA
generativa para parte del arte 2D (ilustraciones de bichos, fondos, iconos
de armas y de logros, e imágenes de la ficha), para asistir en la escritura
del código, y para asistir en la traducción de los textos al inglés. Todo
ese material ha sido revisado, editado e integrado a mano.
El juego no genera contenido con IA durante la partida: no hay ningún
modelo ejecutándose en tiempo real.

Some visual assets used for the Steam store page and marketing materials, including logos, promotional artwork, capsule images, and library assets, were created or assisted using generative AI tools and then reviewed, edited, and finalized by the developer.
No AI-generated content is created during gameplay. AI-generated content is limited to pre-generated promotional and store page materials and does not affect gameplay, game mechanics, or player-generated content.

This game uses generative AI for the following content. All of it was generated during development and shipped with the game; no content is generated at runtime.
- Music and sound effects (2 theme songs, in-game BGM, SFX): Suno
- Graphics (character art, backgrounds, event CGs, store page images): OpenAI
- Extra scenarios, concept and writing: OpenAI, Claude Code
- English text (translation of the main story and extras): Claude Code, OpenAI
- Game implementation (engine, game code): Claude Code

Darrell 3D uses AI-assisted visual assets as part of its art production process, including character artwork, sprites, icons, and FMV-style imagery. These assets were selected, edited, composited, and integrated into the game by the developer.
No generative AI is used during gameplay, and the game does not connect to any external AI services.

Generative AI tool TRAE was used during development to assist in writing portions of the codebase. The visual elements presented in-game — including the target spheres, ground plane, and sky — are directly generated by this code. The generation logic for the ground texture was produced with TRAE and was reviewed and approved by the developer before shipping in the final build. All AI-assisted visual content has been reviewed by the developer to ensure it meets expectations and platform standards. This software does not include any live-generated AI content at runtime.

Generative AI was used to create certain static visual assets, including the “OUTBREAK” text-based logo, the Steam profile background image, and the static background image displayed in the main menu.
No AI-generated content is used during gameplay.

Dubstep: Solar System is an AI-assisted indie game — the studio name, Vibe Coded Reality, wears it proudly. Here is exactly how generative AI was used:
MUSIC: The entire 46-track original dubstep soundtrack was generated with Suno under a paid commercial license, from prompts written by the developer — every track hand-picked from multiple takes and play-tested against the game's beat-gate timing.
CODE: Much of the game's code was written with AI coding assistants working under the developer's direction; all game design, difficulty tuning, and play-testing are human work.
STORE ARTWORK: The cover and capsule artwork were created with AI image tools, then composed and typeset by the developer.
All in-game visuals are drawn procedurally by the game's own code — no AI-generated images appear inside the game itself, and nothing is generated by AI at runtime while you play.

Ironwake contains pre-generated AI content. Some 2D art assets (character sprites, portraits, item illustrations,
backgrounds, and icon sets) were created using AI image-generation tools (PixelLab and MidJourney, plus licensed
third-party icon packs produced with Stable Diffusion). Some sound effects, ambient audio, and music tracks were created
using AI audio-generation tools (ElevenLabs). All AI-generated assets were reviewed, curated, and edited by the
developer. The game does not generate any content with AI at runtime, and no live AI models are accessed by the game.
Some ambient background music tracks used in the game were generated using AI tools. The music is pre-generated and does not change or generate live during gameplay.
AI assistance (a large language model) was used to translate the store page description into English. No in-game assets — 3D models, textures, music, or sound — were created using generative AI.

This game uses AI technology for the following purposes:
- Generation of some assets
- Assistance in text and scenario creation
- Programming assistance for development efficiency
- Efficient automated game testing
No player personal data is sent to AI systems.

In the development of The Duchess Curse, AI tools were utilized as part of the creative workflow. These tools helped generate certain in-game assets, including concept art and thematic imagery, which were then refined and adapted by the developer to fit the game's overall style. Additionally, AI was used in creating atmospheric soundscapes.
These AI-generated sounds served as a foundation, but all audio was carefully edited and refined by the developer to match the specific tone, mood, and immersion of the game. This ensures a personalized and tailored auditory experience that supports the game’s haunting atmosphere.

Some promotional visual assets used on the store page (marketing illustrations) were created with the help of generative artificial intelligence tools.
The game content itself (gameplay, in-game graphics, levels, mechanics, and logic) is entirely created by humans, with no AI-generated content used in real time or in pre-rendered gameplay.

This game uses AI-generated content in limited ways:
The logo was created using ChatGPT.
English voice acting was generated with ElevenLabs.
No other AI tools were used.

Only the JusTD logo, without the text, so basically no A.I. content.
The languages - other than English and Hungarian - were translated using ChatGPT and Google translate!

Some pre-generated visual artwork used in Vitro: Bloodstream (including store artwork) was created with the assistance of generative AI tools and reviewed, edited, and integrated by the developer. No generative AI is used during gameplay or to generate content at runtime.

This game uses generative AI during development for pre-rendered visual assets, store capsule and library artwork, icons, textures, and supporting marketing images. AI-generated material is reviewed and edited before inclusion. The game does not generate AI content for players during gameplay.

This game includes pre-rendered assets created using AI tools. Visual elements have been generated with Playground AI, and voice acting has been created using Genny Lovo AI. These AI-generated assets are used to enhance the game's atmosphere and storytelling. However, the game does not use AI for real-time content generation or gameplay mechanics.

Pre-generated AI tools were used during development to create some 2D visual assets, including in-game sprites, the application icon, and promotional artwork used on the Steam store page. AI tools also assisted with some English and Japanese text and localization. All outputs were reviewed and, where necessary, edited by the developer before being included. The game does not generate AI content during gameplay and does not connect to external AI services.

All graphics and sounds in Woolmates are calculated at runtime by the game itself; no AI-generated image, audio, or video files are delivered. AI assistance tools were used in the development of the program code as well as in text and marketing materials. No AI is used during the actual game.

During development, illustrations (e.g., game over screen) were created using ChatGPT’s image generation features, based on hand-drawn sketches and developer-provided prompts. All AI-generated content was manually reviewed and selected by the developer. No AI is used during gameplay, and no live content or code is generated in-game.

Generative AI was used in the development of this game to assist with the creation of the following content:
1. In-game visual assets: Including background images, scene elements, and icons. Base images were generated using AI image generation tools, then manually selected, modified, refined, and integrated.
2. In-game text and narrative: Portions of dialogue text, story descriptions, and hint messages were generated with assistance from large language models, then manually edited, proofread, and adjusted.
3. Sound effects and music: Some sound effect assets and background music were created using AI audio generation tools, then manually mixed, edited, and optimized.
4. Game program code: Some code snippets were generated with assistance from AI programming tools, then manually reviewed, modified, and integrated.
5. UI interface design: Portions of UI layouts and interface elements were generated with assistance from AI design tools, then manually adjusted and refined.
6. Store page assets: Store cover images, promotional screenshots, and video thumbnails were created using AI image generation tools, then manually post-processed.
7. Marketing and promotional materials: Social media promotional images, marketing copy, and multilingual localization content were generated with assistance from AI tools, then manually reviewed and modified.
All AI-generated content has been reviewed, edited, and integrated by human developers to ensure quality and consistency.
We used generative AI to create some static illustrations, including the title screen and game over screen. The game does not generate AI content during gameplay.

Generative AI was used only to assist in editing and enhancing certain 2D images used in the game, such as improving quality, refining details, or making visual adjustments. All gameplay, programming, game design, and the final implementation of assets were created and reviewed by the developer. No generative AI is used to create gameplay content or player interactions during gameplay.

"Resurrection: The Judgment" incorporates AI technology to enhance the player experience by creating dynamic and immersive gameplay elements.
Pre-Designed AI Content: All visuals, dialogues, and story elements generated with AI have been carefully curated and integrated into the game during development to ensure originality and quality.
No Live AI Interaction: The game does not use live AI systems or external services during gameplay, ensuring a stable and seamless experience.
Enhanced Immersion: AI-generated assets help build a rich and atmospheric world, offering players a deeper connection to the game's narrative and setting.
Our use of AI is guided by respect for creativity and adherence to ethical standards, ensuring all content is unique and tailored to the Resurrection: The Judgment universe.

Generative AI tools were used to create content in this game, including art, sound, in-game text, and the copy on this store page. All of it is reviewed by the developer before release. Nothing is generated by AI while you play.

Used chat got to. Generate 3 pictures for my video story,
1. A yatch sailing on a sea
2. A news paper fake news about the name of the game
3. A news paper fake info saying dream killer related to the narration of the game to immerse the players more into a story view.
All fictional. I used them on the videos.

Generative AI tools were used during development to create or refine some pre-rendered 2D artwork, promotional assets, writing, localization, and development code. All shipped content was reviewed and edited by the developer. The game does not generate content at runtime or connect to external AI services.

Aquasushi Cat was created in collaboration between a human developer and AI tools.
• Music and songs were generated locally using AI (ComfyUI).
• Parts of the game's code — including the code that procedurally draws the hand-styled vector graphics — were written with the help of an AI assistant (Claude).
• The in-game localization (English and Japanese) and store text were produced with AI assistance.
• A small number of sound effects were AI-generated; most sounds were recorded by the developer.
• The store capsule artwork was created with AI image generation (CapCut).
All content was directed, reviewed and finalized by a human developer. No AI content is generated live during gameplay.

Some art assets in this game were created during development with generative AI tools (ChatGPT, Google Gemini, and Leonardo.ai), then manually selected and adjusted by the developer before release.
Music and sound effects are sourced from CC0 assets on OpenGameArt.org and were not AI-generated.

This game uses some pre-rendered UI icons and promotional images created with generative AI tools. No AI is used during gameplay. All in-game content is static and pre-made, with no real-time generation.

Music in the game is created using AI-generated samples.
I also used AI-based tool to assist me with final touch of some environment backgrounds. Specifically as a filter tool to make the lines more shaky.
* Some image textures in the game environment are generated by ChatGPT Image Generator

Some visual assets (pixel art sprites) and music tracks were created with the assistance of AI generation tools during development. All AI-generated content was reviewed and curated by the developer. No AI content is generated during gameplay.

Some of the 2D art in Farmabot — including certain character, creature and crop sprites, cutscene background illustrations, and the game's store page / marketing images (capsules, icon, key art) — was produced with the assistance of locally-run generative AI image tools (Stable Diffusion). All AI-assisted assets are pre-generated (there is no live or runtime AI generation in the game); every asset was curated, edited, and assembled by the developer before inclusion.

Visual assets in this game were initially concepted via AI (Nanobanana2) and then heavily manually edited, overpainted, and pixelated by the developer to ensure a unique aesthetic. Narrative scripts and character voiceovers were developed with AI assistance (Minimax Speech) and manually refined for philosophical depth. No real-time AI content generation is used in the final product.

The pixel art in this game was created with an AI image generation tool (Pixellab).
Generated art is never used as-is: the style, proportions and palette standards are set by a human,
every sprite is reviewed by eye, and anything off-standard is rejected and redone. Grounding,
animation continuity and color consistency are likewise human-checked before adoption.
Game design, balance and specification decisions are made by a human. AI-assisted tools are also
used in the development process.
Nothing is generated by AI at runtime (pre-generated content only).

Generative AI tools were used during development to assist with some pre-generated promotional and graphical artwork used for Cubing Forge, including certain Steam store, library, and marketing assets. All AI-assisted content is reviewed, curated, and finalized before publication. Cubing Forge does not use live generative AI during gameplay.

An AI assistant was used while making this game: the word clues and definitions. Nothing is generated while you play - every puzzle, word and clue is fixed in the build and verified before release. The art is not AI-generated: the capsules, logo and icons are rendered by our own tool from the game's own colours and mark, the interface sounds are by Kenney (CC0) and the music is licensed from Ovani Sound.

This game includes pre-generated content made with the assistance of generative AI tools during development. AI tools were used to help create and iterate some static story illustrations, character and store-art references, voice and sound-effect materials, texture details, copy polishing, and localization drafts. All such content is selected, edited, assembled, and manually reviewed by the developer before shipping. The game does not connect to a live generative AI service during play and does not generate new player-facing AI content at runtime.

This game uses generative AI as part of its development process.
AI-assisted tools were used to help create and refine some visual assets, UI elements, icons, text drafts, and localization drafts. These materials were reviewed, edited, and integrated by the developer before being included in the game.
The game does not generate new AI content in real time during gameplay. All content shown to players is pre-made, reviewed, and included as part of the game build.

Pre-generated key art, store and marketing artwork, and two music loops were created with generative AI tools, then selected, edited, and reviewed by the developer. Gameplay rules, code, interface text, and player actions are authored and deterministic. No content is generated during gameplay, and the game does not connect to external AI services.

Pre-generated AI tools were used during development to assist with the creation of certain 2D illustrations, graphical assets, music, and marketing materials. All generated content was reviewed and selected by the developer before inclusion. The game does not generate AI content during gameplay and does not connect players to any live AI service.

Mars Directive features autonomous AI characters powered by Large Language Models. They don't just generate dialogue—they can observe their surroundings, reason about situations, make independent decisions, interact with the environment, and communicate naturally with both the player and each other. Their behavior is guided by character definitions, gameplay context, and behavioral rules to ensure a consistent gameplay experience.

This game uses generative AI-assisted tools for some pre-generated art and audio assets, including portions of Steam store artwork, character and background assets, the application icon, and some BGM / SFX. All assets are selected, edited, integrated, and tested by the developer. The game does not include live-generated AI content during gameplay, and players will not encounter dynamically generated AI text, images, audio, or other content.

Some plant artwork and store assets were created with AI-assisted tools and then manually reviewed, edited, and integrated into the game. DeskBloom does not generate AI images, text, audio, or other content during gameplay.

Generative AI tools were used during development to create some decorative artwork and surface textures, including botanical table mats and room furnishings. These assets are reviewed and incorporated into the game by the developer. The game does not generate AI content during gameplay or connect to an external AI service.

Dead Air County uses pre-generated AI-assisted content in a limited way.
Generative AI tools were used to help draft and iterate on some store-page text, marketing copy, capsule/store artwork concepts, and some short in-game flavor text such as radio/transmission-style writing. All final content is reviewed, edited, selected, and implemented by the developer before being included in the game or store materials.
Dead Air County does not use live generative AI during gameplay. The game does not generate text, images, audio, levels, characters, or story content dynamically with AI while the player is playing, and no player input is sent to an AI system during gameplay.
AI tools were also used as development assistants for coding, debugging, planning, and workflow support.

Break Even was built with an AI coding assistant working under the developer's direction and review. That includes the game's code and, with it, the pixel maps its sprites are drawn from, its synthesized sound, its dialogue and ending text, the scripts that draw the store images, and drafts of this store page. The game ships no image or audio files of its own — every picture is drawn and every sound synthesized by its own code while you play — and the one bundled file is an open-licence pixel font. No AI runs during play, and the game contacts no AI service.

During the development of the game, generative AI was used as an auxiliary tool to create individual text and graphic materials. All content was checked, edited and integrated manually by the developer. The game does not use generative AI in real time during the passage.

Generative AI tools were used during development to help create early drafts of some game-related content (for example, concept ideas and text drafts). All such content was reviewed, edited, and approved by the developer before release. The shipped game does not generate AI content during gameplay and does not use any external AI services at runtime.

A small number of icons and one minor 3D model were generated with AI tools and then edited by the developer. All AI-assisted assets were reviewed and refined before inclusion. No content is generated at runtime.

Generative AI was used during development to help create visual assets, including characters, cats, environments, story illustrations, animations, and promotional artwork, as well as portions of the writing and localization. These materials were reviewed and edited before inclusion. All AI-assisted content is prepared in advance; the game does not generate AI content during gameplay.

Generative AI tools were used to assist with the creation of some pre-generated visual assets and music used in the game and/or its marketing materials. All AI-assisted content was reviewed and selected by the developer before inclusion. The game does not generate AI content during gameplay.

Some visual assets (creature sprites, plant and background illustrations, and tarot card art, including some store page images) were created using generative AI tools and then curated, edited, and art-directed by the developer. No AI content is generated during gameplay.

AI generated content was used during development for concept art, promotional graphics, marketing materials, and placeholder assets.
The game does not use live AI generated content during gameplay.

Some visual assets in this game and on this store page were made with the assistance of generative AI tools and then edited by hand — specifically, the game's logo and the decorative border of the certificate you are awarded at the end of a run. Everything else was authored by the developer: all other art, all interface text, all film titles, and all game data. Nothing is generated while you play. The game makes no network connection of any kind.

Generative AI tools were used during development to assist with localization, programming, and store/marketing text. All AI-assisted output was reviewed, edited, and integrated by the developer. The game does not use generative AI at runtime and does not generate live AI content.

AI tools were used during development to assist with game code and visual design. The AI helped with coding support, debugging suggestions, and creating certain visual assets such as icons and background elements. No AI-generated content is produced in real time during gameplay — all AI-assisted work was done before release to improve development efficiency and visual quality.

Generative AI was used during development to help create images, background music, and sound effects, assist with programming, and translate in-game text. All voice performances were recorded by human performers. No AI content is generated during gameplay.
ChatGPT helped me write the notes scattered throughout the game, and I made minor modifications to the text. The game icon and splash image are AI-generated.

We use artificial intelligence to generate pre-rendered content for Monochrome Nemesis, including its store page, marketing materials, and community resources. AI helps us optimize and personalize these elements to offer an engaging and unique experience.
I created the card images using ChatGPT. I improved the game's mechanics and visuals using Claude AI.

🎵 In our game, AI is used exclusively for content creation:
• character voice generation,
• sound effects creation,
• background music writing.
AI does not affect gameplay, balance or decision making in the game. All story elements, mechanics and visual content are developed manually.
We used AI tools to generate sound effects, music and voice-overs, but this content is pre-rendered and does not change dynamically during gameplay. No AI is used to live-generate content or code during gameplay.

Some of the game's music and sound effects were created with the help of generative AI tools. Generative AI was also used to create the player avatar images and the gem pack artwork in the in-game store, and to assist with in-game text and its translations into other languages. All AI-assisted content was produced during development and reviewed by the team. The game does not generate any content with AI during gameplay.

Serv-Bot's Firewall uses AI tools in its art and media pipeline, always under human direction and review:
Sprite art. The game's original hand-authored sprites were upscaled and repainted at native resolution with an image-editing model (Qwen-Image-Edit), then reviewed, corrected and in many cases restored to the originals by hand. Concept art for the six "arsenal" enemy types, the Serv-Bot HUD portraits and the achievement icon motifs were generated with local image models (Z-Image Turbo, Qwen-Image-Edit) from our own designs and reference art, then composited and finished in code. Canon elements such as the Greeb ship in the icons are the game's own sprite art, not generated.
Cutscenes. The in-game story videos come from our SIGNAL series. Keyframes were generated with a local image model trained on our own characters, motion with a local video model (Wan 2.2), narration with a text-to-speech model (Kokoro) and music with local music models (ACE-Step, Stable Audio Open). Scripts, story, character designs, editing and direction are ours.
Localization. Interface text in 28 languages was machine-translated with an AI model from our English source and has not yet been reviewed by native speakers.
Code. Parts of the game's code were written with AI coding assistance, reviewed and tested by the developer.
Sound effects are procedurally synthesised, not AI-generated. All AI generation ran on the developer's own hardware; no copyrighted third-party works were used as inputs beyond our own assets and characters.

Generative AI tools were used during development to assist with some 2D background artwork and decorative visual assets. All AI-assisted assets were reviewed and edited before inclusion. The game does not use generative AI during gameplay, and no player input or data is sent to generative AI services. Puzzles and answers are not generated by AI.

Generative AI tools were used during development to assist with character artwork, educational text, translations, musical compositions, and store and marketing materials. This content was prepared during development. The game does not use generative AI during gameplay or connect to external AI services.

Pre-Generated AI was used for:
- Background artwork
- Character illustrations
All AI-generated content was reviewed and edited by the developer.
No Live-Generated AI is used in this game.

Use of Generative AI in the Game
Some in-game assets were created with the assistance of generative AI tools.
Specifically, NPC images were initially hand-drawn by the artist and then finalized and colored using AI-based tools.
Additionally, certain 3D objects appearing in the game were created and refined through AI-assisted production.
No AI is used to generate content dynamically during gameplay.
All AI-assisted content was finalized during the development process and complies with standard Steam store requirements regarding copyright, impersonation, and other applicable policies.
The game icon was created with the use of AI. In addition, some ASCII images seen during gameplay are based on AI-generated imagery.
Some of the game's pre-made content and the store page texts were created with the help of generative AI tools, and then reviewed and edited by our team. No content is generated by AI while you play.

Some shipped artwork and written content were created or assisted with generative AI tools during development. The game does not generate AI content during gameplay and does not connect to external AI services while you play.
This game uses pre-generated AI-assisted visual assets. No live-generated AI content is used.

Some of the text content in this game was produced with the help of generative AI tools, then reviewed and edited by the developer:
- Localization into Ukrainian, Russian, Korean and Simplified Chinese
- Drafting of in-game news headline templates and procedural coin names
All of this content is generated ahead of time and ships as fixed text. The game uses no AI at runtime: it is fully offline, makes no network requests, and generates nothing while you play.
All game systems, market simulation and balance design are the developer's own work.

This is the third iteration of development, that was originally developed in 2019 with HTML + JS, then rebuilt in Unity, and then transferred to LOVE2D written in Lua. It was more-or-less built with a box of scraps in a cave in its first iterations, and modern software since those days have effectively blurred the line where task automation meets unethical AI consumption.
It's up to each of us to determine where that line is for ourselves in a rapidly changing digital age. As both a solo game dev and multimedia artist carrying a full-time job in neither of those fields, I feel that it's important to be educating ourselves on where AI can be a useful tool to allow new opportunities and expand capabilities for independent creators that are otherwise untenable, while keeping the human side of game dev at its core, especially in the indie genre.

Art Assets : Certain visual elements within the game (such as UI icons, background assets, or promotional base art) were created with the assistance of AI image generation tools. All generated images were subsequently redrawn, modified, and stylized manually by the developer to fit the game's aesthetic.
Music & Audio : Some background music or sound effect assets in the game were composed and arranged using AI audio generation tools.
This game does not feature any live-generated AI content (i.e., AI content generated in real-time while playing). All AI-assisted assets were pre-generated during the development phase and carefully reviewed to ensure they do not infringe upon any third-party copyrights.

A Light in the Gloam uses pre-generated AI content. Nothing is generated while the game is running, and the game makes no network calls of any kind.
Visual art: all in-game art was generated with OpenAI's image model (gpt-image-1) from prompts written by hand, then processed by our own scripts, which downscale it, quantise it to a fixed palette and trim it before it is placed in the game. This covers 14 character portraits, 43 enemy and boss sprites, 63 item icons, 27 wall, floor and ceiling textures, 10 dungeon props, 21 achievement emblems, and 14 town and title backdrops. The store capsules and the client icons are crops of the title-screen generation rather than new images.
Music and sound: all 14 music tracks were generated with ElevenLabs' music model and all 47 sound effects with ElevenLabs' sound-effects model, both from written prompts and both post-processed by our own scripts for level and length. There is no voice acting and no synthesised speech anywhere in the game.
Writing and translation: the game's text, meaning item and monster descriptions, dialogue, menus and the story, was written with the assistance of a large language model and then edited by hand. The Brazilian Portuguese translation was produced the same way and reviewed against the English.
